required_work.description: Match the item and lot evidence to the active AFP and its DTSL, date meaning, storage, MRL, and temperature fields.
Calculate required MRL days and actual Remaining Life using the Northstar Receipt Date as day 0.
Determine short-dated versus compliant versus expired status and check for an approved Freshness Exception.
Identify the applicable limit and compare the initial spatially separated product readings.
Verify the expansion trigger, sampling count, and results without averaging away exceptions.
Keep short-date freshness, potential temperature safety/quality concern, and recall authority conceptually separate.
Confirm containment and identify the authority required for technical disposition or release.
Combine the two branches into the current shipment-level state while preserving unresolved decisions.
Communicate facts, calculations, current holds, owners, and next actions without overstating the evidence.

optional_work.description: Have a receiving-capable human verify the recorded visible case date and lot evidence.
Q&R may request vendor loading/cold-room evidence as part of technical disposition.
Explore an FE only if Northstar wants commercial acceptance and all required technical/commercial approvals can be obtained.

acceptable_groupings: AFP identification, MRL arithmetic, and freshness classification may be combined.
Initial and expanded temperature comparisons may be one structured receiving-evidence task.
Hold-state reconciliation and the final shipment summary may be combined.
A specialist may evaluate both branches, but must preserve their distinct policy consequences and authorities.
unnecessary_work: Transportation responsibility analysis; receiving evidence is sufficient and no carrier-causation decision is needed.
Recall execution or store notification because no recall or withdrawal has been declared.
Full supplier facility audit or unrelated product testing review.
